sections.title: Spatial Justice Collective: Study and Praxis in Philadelphia
sections.description:
Through a critical spatial lens, the seminar examines liberatory activism as it emerges from struggles over land, housing, climate, food systems, healing, and democratic governance. Drawing on decolonial, abolitionist, feminist, and anti-capitalist traditions, the course explores how space functions both as a mechanism of institutional violence and as a terrain for collective care, resistance, and world-making.
The course is conceived in solidarity with the Philly Peace Park, whose organizing
principles—direct democracy, land stewardship, abolitionist care, and collective
autonomy—inform the seminar’s pedagogy and ethical orientation. Collective study is
understood not as a supplement to design practice, but as a political and spatial practice in
its own right, grounded in accountability to communities and place.
The seminar begins by establishing a shared framework for examining radical pedagogy, the modern–colonial city, and the role of universities in processes of displacement. From there, the course engages a range of interconnected themes in spatial justice, including housing justice, healing ecologies, climate justice, food sovereignty, solidarity economies, and direct democratic governance. These themes are explored in relation to local and global community struggles, and ongoing efforts to build more just and collectively governed forms of urban life.
